name: SIGNAL/NOISE
description: A deliberately, aggressively analog 3–8 player deduction and social manipulation card game designed as an explicit rejection of BCI-mediated entertainment; the rulebook's introduction states 'no device will help you here' and the game's core mechanic requires players to read facial microexpressions and vocal stress patterns — biological signals inaccessible to digital augmentation. Played widely in anti-connectivity social clubs and among BCI-skeptic communities.
story_hooks: A Signal/Noise player with no BCI augmentation turns out to have illegal geneware enhancing their empathic reading — is that cheating, and does it matter?
The game's anonymous designer surfaces, claiming they originally built Signal/Noise as a training tool for corporate intelligence operatives.
A series of Signal/Noise sessions in a particular bar always end with one player dead within the week — not violently, but dead.
